title: Spell Reviewers work from the Executive Document while the Crafter works from the Executive Sheet
content:
A.1.10.2.4.9.2.2 is one sentence: "For the Reviewers' checks and review of the Spell before deployment, the Executive Document is the primary source of truth for the Spell." Set that against A.1.10.2.4.7.2.2, where "the Crafter must use the Executive Sheet as their key reference document and source of truth."

The two halves of the Spell Team are therefore anchored to *different* artifacts. The Crafter builds from the internal working sheet; the Reviewer checks against the public document voters will read.

This converts review into a genuinely independent path rather than a re-tracing of the Crafter's steps. If the Executive Sheet and the Executive Document have diverged — a late sheet edit, a transcription slip, an item reordered or reworded — code that faithfully implements the Sheet will fail review against the Document. A single shared reference would make that class of error invisible, because both parties would be reading the same possibly-wrong source.

It also puts the check where the commitment lives. What voters authorize is the Executive Document; the Sheet is internal scaffolding. Reviewing against the Document means the final gate asks the governance-relevant question — does this code do what SKY holders were told? — rather than the engineering question of whether the instructions were followed.

The cost is that the Document must be finalized before review (Step 8, Tuesday of week 2, ahead of Step 9), and that later Document changes are tightly restricted: A.1.10.2.4.11.1.3 permits only the address field to be modified after deployment, precisely so the reviewed reference cannot shift underneath the artifact it validated.
description: Anchoring crafting and review to different artifacts means review independently tests Sheet-to-code-to-Document consistency, so a divergence between the two documents cannot pass unnoticed.
